newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says third-quarter profits jump 120 percent.
newsitem.headline: Hilton says third-quarter profits jump 120 percent.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. said Tuesday its profits more than doubled in the third quarter as it parlayed strong results at its full-service hotels with improvements at its Las Vegas casinos.

Hilton said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 jumped 120 percent to $54.5 million, or 28 cents a share, from $24.8 million, or 13 cents a share. The per-share results reflect Hilton's four-for-one stock split last month.

The company, based in Beverly Hills, Calif., said the profit increases resulted from continued strong performances by its full-service hotels and improvements at its Las Vegas operations, especially the Las Vegas Hilton, which rebounded from a disappointing 1995 third quarter.

"Our outstanding third-quarter results demonstrate the pricing power inherent in owning large full-service hotels, such as The Waldorf-Astoria and Hilton Hawaiian Village, as well as the strength of our core Las Vegas gaming operations," President and Chief Executive Stephen F. Bollenbach said in a statement.
Hilton said the primary contributors to the strong performance were its 10 majority-owned or partially owned properties in New York, Chicago, San Francisco, Washington, New Orleans and Honolulu.
It said these "Top Ten" hotels, which had an occupancy rate of 82 percent, continued to benefit from high demand and no new competition in their respective markets.
Hilton said overall occupancy for its hotel division edged up to 77 percent from 76 percent.

During the quarter, Hilton made significant strides in its strategy of acquiring full-service hotels by buying The Prudential Insurance Co.'s interests in the San Francisco, Chicago, New York, Capital, Washington and Rye Town Hiltons for a combined cost of $433 million.
Hilton said its gaming division benefited from strong results at the Flamingo Hilton-Las Vegas, along with generally improved operations at the Las Vegas Hilton.
The company said the Las Vegas Hilton had been adversely impacted in the 1995 third quarter by a significantly lower-than-normal win percentage at its baccarat tables.
Occupancy at Hilton's five hotel-casinos in Nevada increased two points to 90 percent, the company said.
Hilton said its acquisition of Bally Entertainment Corp. continued on track for completion by the end of the year, with the shareholders of both companies approving the transaction in September.
In a related development, Hilton named Bally Chairman Arthur M. Goldberg to run the combined company's gaming operations upon completion of the transaction.
For the first nine months of the year Hilton said its net income increased 37 percent to $150.3 million, or 77 cents a share, from $109.7 million, or 57 cents a share.
Hilton's stock slipped 12.5 cents to $28.125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
